# mdstudio

> mdstudio is a free, open-source, local-first Markdown editor and portability checker. It shows how your Markdown will render on GitHub, dev.to, Obsidian or a strict CommonMark engine, flags syntax that will not travel, and exports clean .md files. Formerly called Markdown Studio.

Write Markdown in a full-featured editor with a complete formatting toolbar and a live preview. The raw Markdown is the single source of truth: the preview shows what other platforms render, with no preview-only syntax. Drafts are saved in the browser (IndexedDB) with no account and are never uploaded unless the writer exports them.

## What it does

- Target profiles: Strict CommonMark, GitHub Flavored Markdown, dev.to, Obsidian. The preview, the checks and the toolbar warnings follow the chosen profile.
- Portability checker: flags raw HTML, local image paths, base64 images, wiki-links, math, Mermaid and trailing-space line breaks, with clickable issues that jump to the line.
- Rich Markdown: tables with cell navigation, task lists, footnotes, GitHub alerts, KaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, syntax-highlighted code blocks.
- Import and export: open .md files, paste from Google Docs, Notion and the web; export clean UTF-8 Markdown (LF endings) or standalone HTML.
- Optional AI writing helpers with the writer's own API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Keys stay in session memory and requests go directly from the browser to the provider.
- Free and MIT licensed. Self-host with Docker (`ghcr.io/deityhub/mdstudio` or `deityhub/mdstudio` on Docker Hub).

## Who it is for

- Technical bloggers publishing to dev.to, Hashnode and static site generators.
- Developers writing READMEs and documentation for GitHub.
- Obsidian users who share notes outside Obsidian.
- Documentation teams who need Markdown that renders the same in every tool.

## Common questions

- Is it free? Yes, free to use in the browser and MIT licensed.
- Are documents private? Yes. They stay in the browser; there is no account.
- How is it different from other Markdown editors? It checks portability across platforms instead of rendering Markdown its own way.
